title: What an Array Is
objectives: Recognize an array as an ordered structure that holds several values of the same type
Understand the concept of an index and that it starts at 0

hook.text: You want to store the grades of 30 students. Will you create 30 separate variables called grade1, grade2, grade3...?

concept.heading: Array: an ordered group of boxes
concept.body: An array holds several values of the same type under a SINGLE name, in order. When you write grades ← [70, 85, 90], one group of boxes named grades is created, and three separate values are lined up inside it.

concept.heading: Index: the address of an element
concept.body: You reach each element in an array through its INDEX (position number). In this lesson and in the Step Runner, arrays start at 0: grades[0] is the first element and grades[1] is the second element. The SIZE of an array (how many elements it holds) is different from its last valid index (size - 1).

workedExamples.prompt: Create an array and reach one of its elements.

steps.explain: The grades array is created with 3 elements: [70, 85, 90].

exercises.question: In the array numbers ← [10, 20, 30], what value is numbers[0]?

feedback.correct: Correct. Index 0 matches the FIRST element of the array.
feedback.incorrect: Arrays start at 0; index 0 points to the first element (10).

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: Index 1 is the SECOND element of the array.

exercises.question: What is the index of the last element of an array with 5 elements?

feedback.correct: Correct. Since it starts at 0, the last index is size - 1: 5 - 1 = 4.
feedback.incorrect: Since arrays start at 0, the last index of an array with 5 elements is 5 - 1 = 4.

exercises.question: What happens if you try to reach array[5] in an array with 5 elements?
options: It gives an out-of-bounds error (the index should have been between 0 and 4)

feedback.correct: Correct. Valid indexes go from 0 to 4; 5 is out of bounds.
feedback.incorrect: In an array with 5 elements, the valid indexes are 0 to 4, so array[5] goes out of bounds.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: The position number of an element in an array is called its ___.

exercises.question: Which structure is the best fit for storing the grades of 30 students?

feedback.correct: Correct. An array holds many values of the same type under a single name.
feedback.incorrect: Instead of 30 separate variables, using a single array (grades[0]...grades[29]) is much easier to manage.

summary: Array: a structure that holds several values of the same type in order under a single name.
Index: the position number of an element in the array, and it starts at 0.
In an array of N elements, the valid indexes go from 0 to N - 1.
